claim_being_audited: The locked action to certify the model without a material weakness disclosure is compliant and adequately supported because aggregate launch readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the affected segment can be treated as non-core.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Non-core or low-volume labels may inform prioritization but do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are named or legal review is pending.
For named launch use-case limitations, disclosure is required unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
evidence_requests: Approved risk-acceptance record explicitly covering the named health-plan benefits support limitation before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the segment gap required disclosure.
Launch materials or model card showing the limitation was actually disclosed, if that occurred.
Contractual or launch-scope documentation clarifying whether the regulated-customer pilot order form made this a named customer commitment.
specific_concerns: The policy text says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the evidence says the affected segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form.
The release-policy note requires disclosure for material limitations in named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the segment gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering the named use-case limitation.
Legal review is still open, which reinforces that the materiality predicate is unresolved rather than satisfied.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents support launch stability, but they do not satisfy the separate disclosure requirement.
unsupported_claims: That the no-disclosure position is adequately supported by the product note calling the segment non-core at 3% of projected traffic.
That general governance guidance on documentation and monitoring is sufficient to justify certification without resolving the named-segment disclosure requirement.
That aggregate launch readiness alone is enough to defend the locked certification decision under the stated policy.
